minutes.headline: PACC elected a chair, vice chair and secretary, and moved its meetings to the library on the first Monday at six.
minutes.summary: The Public Access Cable Committee reviewed minutes, elected officers for a one-year term, heard the manager's report on finances, programming and staffing, and discussed a waiver for staff using personal equipment. It also weighed closed-captioning costs and settled where and when to meet. The next meeting was set for the 14th at six.

public_comment.topic: The chair asked for public comment; none was offered because no members of the public were present.

votes.motion: Approve the meeting minutes, as amended
Elect Steve Walker as chair, Liz Fayetteville as vice chair and Dodge as secretary, on one-year appointments
Meet at the library at six o'clock on the first Monday of each month, or the second Monday if the first is a holiday

budget_items.what_was_said: A member relayed a vendor's estimate for hardware and software installation plus an annual fee for real-time captioning. About 100 hours of real-time captioning was quoted separately.
figures_as_heard: seven to eight thousand dollars a year

budget_items.what_was_said: The manager said FY23 books were not yet closed and the balance would change. April and May interest and the Comcast payment were added.

budget_items.topic: Interest on funds moved to the Bartholomew fund
budget_items.what_was_said: Monthly interest rose sharply after the move, and a member wanted regular reports from the treasurer.
Starting pay is low, and a hire was placed on a higher step through the Personnel committee. Inexperienced candidates start at step one.
Requisitions for FY24 were entered and will convert to purchase orders for supplies and similar items.

decisions.decision: The personal-equipment policy stays adopted pending town counsel review. The manager is to find a generic waiver, and waivers will be requested only as needed.
The enterprise fund status and the Bartholomew reporting were put on the next meeting's agenda.
Next meeting set for the 14th at six o'clock at the library. The first or second Monday will be booked going forward.
The manager will work on recruiting a videographer through job postings, with a suggestion to try active-adult communities.

Captioning costs and the treasurer's reporting on the committee's funds will shape what the committee can spend, though neither was decided.
